correctness.rationale: Cardinal polynomial symmetry uniquely yields weights as linear functions of centered second/fourth moments; exact even-part factorizations, normalization and moment feasibility are proved for every reflection-symmetric probability measure. Beta(a,a) centered moments reduce them to three explicit rational functions; denominator positivity and the quadratic discriminant 1081 give the global sign sets for all real a>0. The first-occurrence claim is checked by explicit exhaustive formulas for all smaller n=1..4. A Python-standard-library verifier reconstructs the cardinal polynomials from rational coefficients and independently checks 280 exact monomial integrations plus symbolic rational identities. Finite checks are supplementary rather than proof of the real-parameter quantifiers.

value.rationale: Fixed-node polynomial-exact weighted integration is a natural numerical problem in which positive coefficients guarantee monotonicity and norm one. The complete feasible two-moment region handles arbitrary symmetric laws; the Beta shape family exhibits two disjoint sharp safe intervals, so increasing concentration can first destroy and then restore quadrature positivity before a second different pair fails. The proof identifies six as the first site count exhibiting this reentrance and yields sharp negative quadrature output for bounded nonnegative data. It is a finite natural classification, not a claim of a new generic coefficient formula or superior approximation accuracy.
